headline: Nvidia Q2 FY27: revenue $96.2B vs $92.17B est; adj EPS $2.22 vs $2.10 est; data center $89.0B vs $85.08B est; guides Q3 revenue $108.0B +/-2% vs $104.19B est and Q3 gross margin 74.0% vs 74.77% est

guidance: No numeric revenue, delivery or margin guidance. Update deck outlook: focused on maximum capacity utilization, with deliveries dependent on demand, supply-chain readiness and allocation between customer sales and Tesla's own fleet; Tesla Semi and Megapack 3 on schedule for production starting in 2026; first-generation Optimus lines being installed at Fremont, with production anticipated later in 2026; over time expects hardware-related profits to be accompanied by an acceleration of AI, software and fleet-based profits. Earnings call: CFO said 2026 capex is still expected to be more than $25B (as projected in April) and will grow for the next two to three years as the robotaxi fleet expands; excluding non-recurring Q1 benefits, automotive gross margin would have been about flat q/q; energy gross margin expected to normalize long term in the low-to-mid 20% range. Musk said robotaxi miles were growing more than 10% a week and expected growth at a high rate through the rest of 2026, and self-driving on Tesla Semi around end-2026 or early 2027.
key_metrics: Automotive gross margin: 16.9% GAAP (Q2 2025: 17.2%); 16.3% excluding regulatory credits (Q2 2025: ~15.0%) vs ~19.4% pre-release Street estimate; total GAAP gross margin 16.8% (Q2 2025: 17.2%) vs 19.5% Tesla company-compiled consensus; regulatory credit revenue $146M (Q2 2025: $439M)

Outlook/guidance statements: no numeric volume or margin guidance; 2026 capex of more than $25B reiterated, rising for the next two to three years; Semi and Megapack 3 production starting in 2026; Optimus production anticipated later in 2026; long-term energy gross margin in the low-to-mid 20% range; continued robotaxi fleet and market expansion through 2026
other_announcements: CFO said Tesla is securing debt facilities that will give it capacity to borrow up to $30B
Update deck: Cybercab production began at Gigafactory Texas; Robotaxi live in seven U.S. metros
headline: Tesla Q2 2026: revenue $28.24B vs $25.71B est; adj EPS $0.33 vs $0.51 est; automotive gross margin ex-credits 16.3% vs ~19.4% est; total GAAP gross margin 16.8% vs 19.5% company-compiled consensus; 2026 capex >$25B reiterated
notes: Consensus differs widely by source: LSEG $25.71B / $0.51 (used); FactSet ~$26.4B / $0.53; Tesla's company-compiled consensus (23 analysts, published July 17) $27.58B revenue / $0.55 non-GAAP EPS / $0.36 GAAP EPS / 19.5% total gross margin / 5.4% operating margin; another tally $25.55B / $0.49. Automotive ex-credit margin estimate: ~19.4% ('Street', per Investing.com) vs ~18.1% (Visible Alpha, cited in a preview). Q2 2025 ex-credit margin (~15.0%) is computed from 10-Q figures.
